A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the momentum transfer rates for collisions between neutral and charged species are not well known and that they are very important in the interstellar medium.

the friction force due to the collisions between charged dust grains and electrons is negligible in the interstellar medium, while the friction between electrons and atomic or molecular ions is significant.
the polarization approximation is a good first-order approximation, which is however not sufficient to describe the friction force in a multi-fluid plasma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the friction force due to collisions between charged species is a nonlinear function not only of the relative drift speed but also of the temperature.
